key_insight: A class-conditioned β-CVAE can generate useful synthetic Raman spectra that improve glioma classification when added to real training data, despite a noticeable synthetic-to-real gap.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help strengthen Raman-based glioma diagnostics in small, imbalanced patient cohorts where collecting enough real spectra is difficult.
method: Trained a β-conditional variational autoencoder to generate Raman spectra by glioma class.
Evaluated both IDH binary classification and 6-class methylation subtype classification.
Compared train-on-synthetic and real-plus-synthetic augmentation under patient-isolated cross-validation, including a reconstruction-based classifier.
evidence_signal: Across 58 tumor samples, synthetic-only models underperformed real-data models, but adding synthetic spectra consistently improved downstream classification in the reported evaluation.
watch_item: The synthetic spectra do not fully match real data distributions, so augmentation should be used cautiously and validated with patient-isolated testing.
paper_title: Generative Augmentation of Raman Spectra for Glioma Classification
